text:
Eli: quick thought — we keep hitting disruptive tenant egress IP churn during private endpoint failovers. What if we switch to a short-lived lease model with a heartbeat from the tenant agent to extend? Lease expires only after a grace window, so NAT/SNAT bindings don't vanish instantly.

Priya: interesting. Lease + heartbeat would let us avoid mid-request IP flips. We should define: lease TTL, heartbeat interval, and a max-extensions cap. Also need metrics for extension rate. :bar_chart:

Sam: concern: NAT exhaustion on shared pools. If leases are long and many tenants flapping, we could run out of ephemeral IPs. Need eviction heuristics (LRU or rate-based) and a way to preempt low-priority tenants.

Jorge: +1 to eviction policies. Proposal: tag leases with priority and last-active timestamp. Eviction order: expired -> lowest-priority -> longest-idle. Also expose a tenant-facing header so clients can opt into graceful fallback routing.

Eli: sketch for lease state in control plane:
```
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "egress_ip": "198.51.100.22",
  "lease_expires_at": 1710000000,
  "priority": "standard",
  "extensions": 2
}
```
Heartbeat extends TTL if extension cap not exceeded.

Priya: operational playbook items: 1) alert when extension rate > threshold 2) autoscale ephemeral pool 3) dashboard showing eviction ops. Also, what about routing propagation — we might need to delay route deletion by X seconds after lease expiry to avoid packet blackholes.

Sam: routing delay is good. But we should avoid long delays that cause sticky IPs. Maybe: immediately stop advertising for new sessions but honor flow continuation for 30s by keeping SNAT entry on the box. That avoids tearing TCP/HTTP keepalive.

Jorge: fallback modes: a) regional relay (proxy) b) route to alternate egress pool c) immediate fail-close. Recommend default = regional relay for high-SLA tenants, with config knob per-account.

Eli: security question — when a lease expires and is reallocated, ensure OLD tenant's packets cannot be forwarded. Need deterministic flow teardown: revoke conntrack entries + rotate SNAT mapping. Documented script/ops steps required.

Priya: also KMS/key material rotation for the sidecar tokens used in heartbeat. Heartbeat auth must be short-lived and auto-rotated.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: perf-test job queued: test/egress-lease-heartbeat-spike (est ~2h).

Sam: one more tricky bit: cross-account peering and overlapping CIDRs. If we rely on ephemeral IPs that may be in customer CIDR ranges, routing conflict. We should constrain ephemeral pool to provider-owned /24s only; avoid customer-supplied blocks.

Jorge: operationally, add a dry-run flag for the rollout: start with a single region and a handful of tenants, collect metrics for extension churn and eviction frequency.

Eli: next steps: 1) write mini-RFC covering lease model + eviction policy + heartbeat auth 2) prototype agent heartbeat + CP lease table (spike) 3) run perf test (infra-bot). I'll draft RFC and share. Any objections?

Priya: no objections. Add a section for observability (per-tenant lease history + reason on eviction).

Sam: fine. Add explicit escape hatch to disable leases per account.

Jorge: 👍 will help draft eviction ordering and fallback routing snippets.

Eli: thanks — will post RFC later today. :tada:
